https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1375#issuecomment-3969687786 - this might be relevant. It seems that chrome might be subtracting the outline-width value from outline-offsets value when using outline-style auto. It seems this is done past computed style time, potentially it's just part of paint?

I think applying a negative outline offset is acceptable?

That being said the fact outlines get clipped is actually rather unfortunate.

On my WebKit build (MiniBrowser), I can control the initial offset with outline-width. As I understand it, it works like this: The outline is drawn before the outer outline area defined by `outline-width`. The outline line itself has a width of 2px, which ignores zoom. Example: `outline-width: 5px` (The blue solid outline is there for reference; it is 5px and is affected by zoom.) If `outline-width` is smaller than the line width, the line is drawn just outside the inner area defined by `outline-width`: Example: `outline-width: 0px` So if I want to place the outline just inside a box, I set `outline-width` to a value, and the `outline-offset` to its negative, for example: `outline-width: 2px; outline-offset: -2px`, (which is different from `outline-width: 0px; outline-offset: -2px`). A little while ago, I opened an issue in CSSWG about this: https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13587

I think @nt1m has the right idea (elsewhere) and ideally we standardize upon

```
select option:focus-visible { outline-offset: inset }
```

with `inset` being a new value that's essentially zero minus the auto style width.
That sounds like the best approach. Also means people are free to use it elsewhere.

If a user applies a style that increases the size of all outlines (and applies `outline-style: solid`), and the website uses `inset` to solve an `overflow: hidden` scenario (instead of a negative offset), could there be a risk of content being obscured by the outline?

Or if a UA has a larger-than-usual `outline-style: auto` width?
I think that risk always exists. `inset` should maybe simply be the inverse of `outline-width`.
As far as I know, that risk currently exists only in WebKit. ```css outline: auto 5px blue; outline-offset: -5px; ```` Adding `outline-style: solid;` to the style above:
That's just kinda inherent to using auto I think. It's explicitly implementation-defined.

Kinda. The current WebKit implementation doesn't pass this test:
https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-ui/outline-auto-width-001.html

That seems like a bug to fix. Probably not too hard now that we changed some of how we handle outline around.

That did make me realize that the computed value of `inset` has to be `inset`, at least as long as the style is `auto`.

> That seems like a bug to fix

Thanks!, this answer a question I asked in https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13587#issuecomment-4042787634

---

Another question regarding WebKit's auto outline:
> Is it intended that the width does not scale with zoom?

---

When one uses a negative `outline-offset`, it indirectly implies that a **specified** portion of the focused element can be obscured without compromising the visibility of the content.
This allows the style and width of the outline to be changed safely without affecting the visibility of both the content and the outline.

`inset` alone doesn't do that.

I fixed auto outline zoom the other day, so no.

I'm not really sure what you're trying to say with your last couple of sentences. I think we need something like `inset` for the problem at hand. Hard-coding specific values is kind of antithetical for the `appearance: base` effort and I don't think we want to figure out a way to draw `outline` on the outside despite `overflow: auto`. I'm open to other suggestions though.

> I fixed auto outline zoom the other day, so no.

Thanks! Now waiting for the other `outline-width` thing. I'm curious to know how it will be fixed.

---

> I'm not really sure what you're trying to say with your last couple of sentences

Just that content will be obscured for users who use a large outline width.

---

> Hard-coding specific values is kind of antithetical for the appearance: base effort

I'm not sure if that's the case, but you're probably right.

---

> I don't think we want to figure out a way to draw outline on the outside despite overflow: auto

For certain.

---

> I'm open to other suggestions though.

(I don't know about the syntax)
`outline-offset: inset {min-offset};`
`outline-offset: inset -0.25em;`: Tries to place the outline inside the box (negative offset) and caps the offset at `-0.25em`.

`outline-offset: inset;`: Tries to place the outline inside the box (negative offset) and caps the offset at a default minimum value of `- medium`.

getComputedValue returns max(- outline-width, min-offset)
That seems like way too much complexity just for the auto value which all user agents have at 3px or less.
It's not only for auto values
In all the other cases you have direct control over the width.
Are you saying users who want large :focus-visible outlines should accept the downsides of outline-offset: inset?

I tried solving **my** issue directly in the userstyle; maybe this could work: 
```css
outline-width: if(style(outline-offset: inset): medium; else: 15px; );
```

I can see in chrome that the focus ring is partially clipped by the picker, I never noticed before because only a little bit of it is clipped. If Anne and Tim's [proposed fix](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12286#issuecomment-4136691857) works and everyone is happy with it then I am supportive.

Is there a CSSWG issue for the proposed inset value? It seems like it should be easy enough to specify (given it's mostly just do the right thing for your given UA styles), and would be good to get in chromium and firefox too.
Filed https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13765.

The CSS Working Group just discussed `outline and ::picker(select)`, and agreed to the following: * `RESOLVED: Accept outline-offset: inset keyword, it computes to the keyword, and use it on base appearance options.`
The full IRC log of that discussion <jarhar> annevk: *gives intro*
<lwarlow> The CSSwg issue for the proposed inset value: https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13765
<keithamus> RRSAgent, please draft minutes v2
<RRSAgent> I have made the request to generate https://www.w3.org/2026/04/16-css-minutes.html keithamus
<lwarlow> q+
<astearns> ack lwarlow
<jarhar> lwarlow: i agree, i think that the inset value makes sense and solves the problem quite neatly
<jarhar> lwarlow: i can see that there could be issues in certain cases where the outline might end up clipping hte content of whatever has the outline
<jarhar> lwarlow: for options that wont be an issue because of the padding
<jarhar> lwarlow: if we use it for other things in the future then you can account for tiny bit of padding somewhere
<jarhar> lwarlow: would it compute to the inset keyword?
<lwarlow> Ship it
<jarhar> annevk: yeah. currently in webkit it doesnt because were trying to hide it. if we standardize it then it should compute as a keyword
<jarhar> astearns: there hasnt been any discussion on the css issue yet. the first thing that comes to my mind, if we have this keyword, its now something that authors can use everywhere. is that going to cause any issues?
<jarhar> annevk: its the same as if they took the width value, negated it, and put it on outline-offset. its alreayd possible. its only really novel for auto because for auto you dont know the width
<jarhar> annevk: for chrome youd have to use -0.5px, and for webkit youd have to use -3px
<jarhar> astearns: the keyword would give that to you
<jarhar> annevk: i think overall its a win. you dont have to ua sniff for the negated value for auto
<flackr> q+
<jarhar> astearns: are we deciding here to endorse this new value for outline offset and use it in this case for appearance base?
<jarhar> flackr: i wanted to ask if we have considered something more radical like not clipping outlines? outlines are already outside of some of the regular box painting
<jarhar> flackr: from a developers perspective, there are many things we can honor to outline things in a scrollable container
<lwarlow> q+
<astearns> ack flackr
<jarhar> annevk: it would probably get a lot more complicated if you wanted to draw outside. youd need a new layer. it would be more expensive and deal with the interaction with the scrollbar
<jarhar> annevk: i definitely thought about it, it would be nice, but doesnt feel very pragmatic
<jarhar> flackr: yeah its already the case that the outline goes on top of other things that you wouldnt paint on top of like ancestor borders
<jarhar> flackr: i dont claim to have a complete idea here, but it seems like the developer friendly thing would be to not reserve space for the outline
<jarhar> annevk: i did find at least one other scenario where outline required a new layer but we didnt use one. if the border has blending, all UAs do something wrong where the blending bleeds into the outline
<jarhar> annevk: that path also has risky perf implications
<astearns> ack lwarlow
<jarhar> lwarlow: i dont think theyre mutually exclusive. as a value this makes sense to add
<jarhar> lwarlow: i havent experienced the outline clipping in scroll containers and being really annoyed by it
<jarhar> lwarlow: the behavior seemed inconsistent between browsers
<jarhar> lwarlow: with this value i could get it consistent
<jarhar> lwarlow: if we could solve that separately that would be great but it doesnt need to block this
<lwarlow> Proposed Resolution: Accept outline-offset: inline keyword, it computes to the keyword, and use it on base appearance options.
<jarhar> flackr: yes we can pursue both. this is a nice simple short term fix
<lwarlow> Proposed Resolution: Accept outline-offset: inset keyword, it computes to the keyword, and use it on base appearance options.
<jarhar> +1
<jarhar> RESOLVED: Accept outline-offset: inset keyword, it computes to the keyword, and use it on base appearance options.
<jarhar> astearns: i suspect that we may talk about this separately in csswg
<jarhar> annevk: this could just apply to option elements without needing to consider base appearance
<jarhar> astearns: trying to think whether there would be any web compat issues
<jarhar> annevk: if people looked at computed style and branched their code
<dbaron> jarhar: [ something about how options aren't focusable except when outside select so this is ok if we just make the selector match only options in a select ]
